chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfaly, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'The bird, when it takes control of its wings, is prey, and it is permissible for the one who seizes it.'

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful, a title for Imam Ali (peace be upon him).
key_terms.صَيْدٌ: Prey or game; an animal caught for food.
key_terms.مَلَكَ جَنَاحَيْهِ: To take control of one's wings; implies being airborne and active.

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a bird to be considered halal prey in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi clarifies the specific condition for a bird to be considered 'sayd' (game) and thus halal, emphasizing that mere possession is insufficient; the bird must be airborne and actively controlling its wings. In Shia jurisprudence, this distinction helps differentiate between wild game and domesticated birds, ensuring the ruling applies only to creatures capable of independent flight and capture. The narration links the Prophet's wisdom to Imam Ali, reinforcing the practical application of hunting laws in daily life.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The bird, when it is in control of its wings, so it is a hunted prey, and it is Permissible for the one who seizes it’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that ’Amir al-Mu 5 minin has said, ‘The birds which have full control over their wings, belong to whoever catches them and they are lawful for them . 555
